entries.title: Seeded Crystal Lattice Growing in a Solution Box
entries.description: A small cube “seed crystal” at the center of a transparent box of floating ions that randomly move, collide with the seed, and snap into a growing cubic lattice, with attached ions glowing briefly and a counter showing lattice size.

entries.title: Snowflake Branching from a Single Nucleus
entries.description: A tiny hexagonal nucleus in the center where water molecules drift in from a mist, attach only at certain angles to form branching hexagonal arms, with tips glowing blue as they grow and a slider to change temperature (attachment probability).

entries.title: Crystal Growth Against a Rock Wall
entries.description: A rough, fixed rock wall mesh where mineral particles in a flowing transparent fluid slowly attach, forming faceted crystals that protrude outwards, with color changing from faint to vivid as each crystal gets larger.

entries.title: Lattice Defects and Dislocation Motion
entries.description: A 3D grid of spheres forming a perfect crystal where a few missing atoms (vacancies) and extra atoms (interstitials) can wander, collide, and move along, with dislocation lines highlighted in red and a stress meter that, when increased, makes defects glide through the lattice.

entries.title: Layer‑by‑Layer Epitaxial Film Growth on a Substrate

entries.title: Crystal Dissolution vs. Growth in Changing Solution

entries.title: Ionic Crystal Formation from Oppositely Charged Ions
entries.description: Red and blue charged spheres drift and bounce gently in a box, then snap into place when they approach a growing NaCl‑like lattice seed, forming alternating colors in all directions, with faint electric field lines drawn around the forming crystal.

entries.title: Crystal Under Mechanical Stress Fracturing Along Planes
entries.description: A rectangular crystal block with visible lattice planes is slowly bent by two moving paddles; as stress increases, cracks nucleate on specific lattice planes, propagate in straight lines, and split the crystal into pieces that detach and fall with trails.

entries.title: Metallic Crystal Melting and Recrystallizing
entries.description: A close‑packed lattice of spheres jitters slightly at low “temperature,” then jiggles more violently as a temperature slider rises, causing the lattice to dissolve into a liquid; lowering the slider lets atoms reattach, nucleate new crystals, and grow polycrystalline regions with distinct colors.
